Laura — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers from our side:
- Staging index: ~540k documents, avg text length ~220 tokens. We have a few larger blobs (~2% over 2k tokens).
- Vector DB: Milvus v2.3, 6-node k8s cluster (each node: 64GB RAM, 8 vCPU). Current sustained upsert throughput ~600 ops/s; peak bursts to 1.2k for short periods.
- Canary sample: 2k queries for 24h works for us; prefer Tue/Wed window to align with EngOps staffing.
- Blackouts: monthly maintenance window is first Saturday of the month — avoid that.

Couple of asks from our side before we lock the window:
1) Do you have a recommended throttling curve for bulk backfill to avoid OOM on Milvus?
2) We need a short runbook for rollback steps that non-Redwood engineers can follow.

Alex / team — adding the implementation POV and backfill guidance. High-level: we recommend a staged bulk + streaming approach to avoid saturating Milvus memory and to keep query latency stable. Notes:

- Backfill throughput guidance:
  • Start at 200–300 upserts/s for the first 2 hours, monitor memory & flush times.
  • If stable, ramp by 20% every 30 minutes until you reach 800 upserts/s.
  • Hold at burst up to 1k ops/s only for short (10–15 min) intervals; Milvus observed peaks but sustained >800 causes compaction pressure.

- Batch sizing: 128–512 vectors per batch depending on record size. For larger docs chunk into smaller vectors.

- Sharding / replica guidance: for Milvus on k8s, a 3-shard layout with 2 replicas reduces tail query impact; ensures single-shard compactions don't kill read latency.

- Fallback strategy: Redwood's serving runtime can route to a rerank-disabled variant (search-only) if a node crosses a memory/latency threshold; plan for a ~5% traffic fallback initially.

- Pre-checks: ensure embedding dimension (768) matches model output; we saw an earlier mapping mismatch in embed-mapping-v1 — the attached CSV is v2 with corrected type annotations.

- Runbook stub (short):
  1) Pause backfill job.
  2) Verify Milvus memory & compaction logs.
  3) If OOM risk: reduce batch size to 64 and drop to 200 ops/s.
  4) If node failure: mark node unschedulable, let replicas serve, continue backfill at reduced rate.

I've attached milvus-capacity-estimates.xlsx with rough memory forecasts and a simple python upsert snippet we can share in the ops call.

-ben

Hi all — adding the acceptance criteria and rerank eval plan so we have clear gates for the staged rollout. Keep these high-level so EngOps can run them independently.

Acceptance gates (staging):
- Data parity: embedding count in staging matches source count ±0.1% after backfill completion.
- Smoke latency: 95th percentile query latency stays within 1.5x current prod baseline for the canary traffic.
- Rerank quality: MRR on the eval suite does not drop by more than 1.5% vs baseline; precision@5 should be within ±2%.
- Error budget: no more than 0.5% error responses related to embedding lookups or ranker failures during the 24h canary.

Rerank eval plan:
- Use the attached rerank-eval-suite.zip (2k prompts + labels). Run two runs: pre-cutover (baseline) and post-backfill. Compute MRR, precision@k, and a small human spot-check (10 random queries).
- If quality delta is >1.5% MRR regression, hold and trigger post-mortem.

Rollout checklist for day-of:
1) Preflight: dry run of upsert on a 5k subset with monitoring hooks.
2) Start bulk backfill with Ben's throttling curve.
3) Enable canary traffic to rerank variant for 2k queries.
4) Run eval harness (should take ~45 minutes).
5) If all gates pass, proceed to phased traffic increase 10% -> 40% -> 100% over 6 hours.

Rollback quick steps (for EngOps):
- Disable rerank variant (route to search-only).
- Pause backfill; reduce batch size; investigate compaction logs.

I'll draft a short runbook doc in Drive and post the link after this thread.

Thanks — Monica
